response.rationale: R1 directly explains proximal weakness and dysphagia via hyperthyroidism (suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, anti-thyroglobulin) and history of thyroiditis; normal CK and EMG are consistent. R5 lacks thyroid function evidence and has low-titer ANA; R2 is contradicted by normal CK/EMG; R3 and R4 do not explain muscle weakness.

rejected.why: Contradicted by normal creatine kinase and normal electromyography, which are inconsistent with inflammatory myopathy.
Sacroiliitis and thigh edema are present but do not explain the proximal muscle weakness or thyroid abnormalities.
Joint stiffness and tenderness are present but do not account for the progressive muscle weakness or thyroid dysfunction.
